title: Include timestamp-zero events in replay reconstruction without duplicate forward playback
description:
## Finding

Recording retains output at elapsed millisecond zero, but reconstruct omits it. This affects normal center panes, independently of filtered corner streams.

## Evidence

Baseline 299fc13, crates/thegn-host/src/replay.rs:213-225. reconstruct initializes a fresh emulator then calls feed_into(emu, 0, at_ms). feed_into skips ev.at_ms <= from_exclusive, including every event during the first millisecond. search_next and export_cast include those same events.

Standalone audit reproduction /tmp/thegn-audit/replay-probe/replay.rs::audit_epoch_zero_is_exported_and_searchable_but_not_reconstructed appends A at recording.epoch. The ring has one event at 0, exported cast contains A and search finds it at 0, but reconstruct(0) is blank. Root reran the four reproduction tests; all assert current broken behavior, not fixes.

## Impact

Initial prompt/output and initial resize events can disappear from replay. Search can select a timestamp whose reconstructed grid lacks the matched text. Tests based on immediate feed/reconstruct are timing-dependent.

## Acceptance

* Distinguish reconstruction from the start of retained history from forward playback strictly after an already-consumed event; timestamp 0 is a valid time, not an uninitialized sentinel.
* Include all events at/before requested time during reconstruction, including multiple events at 0.
* Preserve exactly-once incremental playback across same-millisecond event groups, paused seek and resumption; use event sequence identity if timestamps cannot express the cursor.
* Deterministic tests cover bytes and resizes at 0, multiple events sharing timestamps, reconstruct(0), search/reconstruct agreement, repeated feed intervals and backward seek. No sleeps to shift events away from 0.

## Dependencies

Independent baseline defect; related THE-548's center-replay regression coverage must not hide it with delays. No disk-format migration is required for the memory-only ring.
